title: a merge card animates its logic and walks the key diff blocks: the spec explain carries an optional scene (lanes, nodes, edges, runtime tokens and numbered changes) that the board lays out and animates as before → change → after; the reviewer's verdict text carries one fenced walk that explains at most five key blocks per intent, bound to the reviewed head, while every other hunk is listed by file; each intent row links into its changes and its key blocks, and a walk from another head is shown as out of date
acceptance: Why and reference, self-contained. The captain approved the board prototype on 2026-10-07: "看板樣式可以了, 可以以這個版本開發". Before that the captain asked, verbatim: "引領我們看代碼時, 能否在網頁上逐行或逐區塊解釋代碼運作邏輯?"; "逐塊解釋可以的話, 可以畫出解釋邏輯的動圖"; "整個大的before/after diagram也可以改造成動圖, 不要只有固定的上到下的長方體堆疊, 要能真的畫出邏輯變化"; "你的決定這個區塊佔用太多版面寬度, 希望善用這個區塊導引看diff產生更多動圖說明每一段code block"; "船員名冊顯示的太窄, 高度太限縮, 閱讀順序應該是先看意圖重點列表, 再帶到動畫邏輯帶看". Later, verbatim: "有些單向門我們初步只想看證據的時候, 細節的程式碼解釋可以先藏起來, 真的有需要看才點開" and "現在 140 / 239 兩百多段code snippet船長是沒辦法看的, 應該先出現意圖分頁, 就重點的意圖的幾點去做代碼解釋和動畫". This spec is normative on its own: every shape, limit and rendering rule below replaces the prototype brief, which is reference only and not needed to implement or review this task. Prerequisite: T-242 (merged as d9cba7a, PR #254) supplies the evidence-first merge card this task extends: the explain fields change_points/door/check validated by bin/lib/fm_ste.py _walk (:143-193), their injection from the approved pinned spec into merge-card details by bin/lib/fm_card_refs.py prepare_details (:220-243) called from bin/fm-decide.sh (:495-545), the read-only exact-head diff parser fm_card_refs.parse_diff (:98-182) and the `refs` it attaches, and the board's intentBody/changeWalk rendering (board/public/index.html:1257-1323). The explain contract this extends is design/design.md §5.2 (:422-440).

Change 1, the scene schema (bin/lib/fm_ste.py check_explain/_validate, bin/lib/fm_spec_preflight.py). explain.<locale> may carry an optional `scene`; when present it is required in both locales. Shape: `lanes` (1-6 items, each {label}); `nodes` (1-24 items, each {id, label, lane, kind, state, change?}); `edges` (0-40 items, each {id, from, to, state, change?, label?}); `tokens` {before: [edge ids], after: [edge ids]}; optional `counter` {label, before, after}; `changes` (1-9 items, each {id, text, intents}). Rules: a lane is referenced by its 0-based array index (integer, in range). Node and edge ids match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,23}$ and are unique across nodes and edges; change ids are exactly c1..cN in order (they are the numbered badges). kind ∈ input|step|decision|store|focal|oneway; node and edge state ∈ same|gone|new. `change` is required when state is gone or new and must name an existing change id; it is forbidden when state is same. Edge from/to name existing node ids; an edge touching a gone node is gone, an edge touching a new node is new, and no edge joins a gone node to a new node. tokens.before and tokens.after are each 1-24 edge ids forming a continuous path (edge[i].to == edge[i+1].from; repeats allowed to write out loops); before uses only same|gone edges, after only same|new edges. counter.label follows the node-label rules; counter.before and counter.after are 1-12 code point strings, not STE-checked. changes[].intents is a nonempty list of 1-based indexes into that locale's explain intent list, without repeats. STE: lane, node and edge labels and counter.label are checked by the existing label path (fm_ste.label, the same limits as before_nodes labels); each changes[].text is exactly one STE fact sentence (fm_ste.check, kind fact). Locale agreement: the lane count, every node and edge id with its lane, kind, state, change, from and to, the tokens, counter.before/after, and every change id with its intents are identical across en and zh-TW, in the same order; only label and text values differ. before_nodes/after_nodes stay required and remain the fallback. No coordinates and no layout file are stored or written: bin/fm-diagram.sh, board/public/diagram.js and the authored HTML diagrams are unchanged. A scene violation is refused by `fm_ste.py check-explain` and by spec preflight with a specific message naming the field. The task-file validator in bin/lib/fm_config_tasks.py (:35-40) calls the same check_explain and needs no change.

Change 2, scene delivery to cards (bin/lib/fm_card_refs.py, bin/fm-decide.sh). The authoritative source of a merge card's scene is the task's approved pinned spec explain, read exactly as fm-decide already reads the pin for the T-242 fields (bin/fm-decide.sh:495-503). fm-decide injects explain.<locale>.scene into details.<locale>.scene for every merge request whose pinned spec has a scene, whether the details were authored or built by bin/lib/fm_merge_details.py from the dispatch card (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:655-661); this injection does not depend on the spec having change_points. Authored details that carry a scene different from the pin are refused with 'scene mismatch with spec'; authored details may omit it. prepare_details adds 'scene' to the fields it copies and compares (fm_card_refs.py:227). bin/lib/fm_merge_details.py is unchanged: its INTENT_FIELDS (:9) still excludes scene, and fm-decide supplies it after the build. Task detail (board/server.ts:2454-2466) already serves spec.explain, so a scene reaches the task detail view without a server change.

Change 3, the walk the reviewer writes (bin/fm-review.sh, skills/reviewer/SKILL.md). For a code review of a task PR (not spec preflight), the review prompt asks for at most one fenced block with info string `walk` inside the verdict final text, holding JSON {"intents": [{"intent": N, "key": [block, ...]}]} where a block is {"hunk": id, "kind": "code"|"test", "note": {"en": s, "zh-TW": s}, "line_note"?: {"line": n, "en": s, "zh-TW": s}, "proves"?: [hunk ids], "changes"?: [change ids], "step"?: {"nodes": [ids], "edges": [ids]}}. The reviewer does not list the other hunks: they are computed (Change 4). The diff the reviewer is shown (bin/fm-review.sh:894) becomes exactly `git diff --no-ext-diff --no-color --no-renames <base> <head>`, the same rename rule as the patch binding (:394), and the raw diff block stays a contiguous, unannotated diff; directly after it the prompt adds a section '## Hunk ids' with one line per id, `<id>  <@@ header line>` (binary, mode and empty ids with their kind), so the reviewer copies ids rather than computing them. The walk crew_status line is emitted once, immediately after the verdict's existing crew_status line, so a review's event sequence becomes review_opened, crew_status, approved|review_failed, crew_status, crew_status (walk), agent_finished. tests/review-diff.test.sh (:55-72, :133) is updated to the new golden prompt (the --no-renames diff followed by the hunk-id section) and the new exact event sequence; its source-binding, checkout and identity assertions are unchanged. After the verdict is retained, fm-review runs `fm_walk.py check` on the retained final text and emits one bilingual crew_status line naming only the status and a fixed reason category (for example 'unknown hunk id' or 'note fails STE'), never a path, an excerpt or note text; when the verdict is posted as a PR comment (the comments projection, bin/fm-review.sh:1323-1330), the posted text has the walk fence replaced by one line 'Code walk retained with the evidence (N key blocks).' while the retained evidence record keeps the full text; the verdict, its markers, its signature, its provenance and fm-review's exit status are never changed by the walk. The fence is already excluded from verdict-marker parsing (bin/lib/fm_evidence.py unquoted/verdict_marker, :26-46).

Change 4, hunk identity and coverage (new bin/lib/fm_walk.py, reusing fm_card_refs.parse_diff). The canonical diff is the Change 3 git diff between the retained verdict record's base and head, computed by the trusted outer process, never by the reviewer. parse_diff gains an option that keeps every hunk row typed: rows are {type: add|del|ctx, old: line or null, new: line or null, text} in diff order (a mixed replacement hunk keeps both its del and add rows); without the option its current output is unchanged. A text hunk's id is `<path>#R<start>-<end>` on the new side, or `<path>#L<start>-<end>` for a deletion-only hunk, where start/end are the inclusive 1-based lines on that side exactly as parse_diff computes them; a deleted file's hunks are therefore L ids. Renames do not occur (--no-renames: a rename is a deletion plus an addition). A binary file, a mode-only change and an empty added or deleted file have no text hunk: they get the single id `<path>#binary`, `<path>#mode` or `<path>#empty` and can never be key. A submodule change is an ordinary text hunk. `other` is computed, never written: one entry per changed file not fully covered by key blocks, {file, hunks: number of its ids not used as key, kinds: [binary|mode|empty] when applicable}, files unique and sorted, so key ∪ other covers every id exactly once by construction. Validation of the walk (fm_walk.check): exactly one walk fence (two or more → invalid 'duplicate walk'); valid JSON object with only the key `intents` (else invalid); intents entries unique by intent, each intent an integer 1..len(spec explain intent); every key hunk id exists in the canonical diff and is key at most once across all intents; at most 5 key blocks per intent and at most 40 in all; kind is code or test; note has exactly the keys en and zh-TW, each exactly one STE fact sentence; line_note, if present, has exactly line/en/zh-TW, its line is a row of the block on the block's side (an add or ctx row's new number for an R id, a del or ctx row's old number for an L id), and each text is one STE fact sentence; proves only on test blocks, naming key blocks of kind code in the same walk; changes name scene change ids whose intents include the block's intent; step is required for every key block when the card's pinned spec has a scene and forbidden when it has none, and names at least one existing scene node or edge id. A PR of any size can be walked: only key blocks carry notes, and a 400-hunk diff with 3 key blocks is valid.

Change 5, walk storage, selection and attachment (bin/lib/fm_walk.py, bin/fm-decide.sh). No new evidence record kind and no change to bin/lib/fm_evidence.py: the walk is extracted on demand from the retained verdict record's text through the existing reader (Store.verdicts, :243-247), so it is bound to that record's head, base and patch and its signature exactly as the verdict is. For every merge request, enriched or not, fm-decide runs `fm_walk.py attach` after the T-242 refs step (when there is one) and before the card is written; the existing refs-helper refusal (bin/fm-decide.sh:520) is unchanged and the walk adds no refusal of its own. attach builds details.walk: {status: valid, head, base, patch, intents: [{intent, key: [block + file, side, start, end, rows, url]}], other: [...]} when its walk validates; {status: absent|invalid, head, reason} when that record has no walk or an invalid one; {status: stale, reviewed_head} when no APPROVE verdict exists at the expected head but an older one exists (for example a same-patch rebase that carried approval). A block's rows come from the trusted local diff. A hunk of at most 80 rows is shown whole; a longer hunk shows an 80-row window, starting at its first row, or, when it has a line_note, the window whose start is max(0, min(row index of the line note - 40, total - 80)), so the noted line is always inside it; the block then carries truncated {before: k, after: m}, the counts of omitted rows, and the board says so. The url is parse_diff's PR file anchor. Selection and failure, exhaustively, and fm-decide's exit status and card writing are unaffected in every row: (1) fm_walk.py unreadable → details.walk {status: unavailable, reason: 'walk helper missing'}; unlike the refs helper, the walk never refuses a request; (2) no verdict record for the task (for example an external-only review policy, bin/lib/fm_binding.py:277) → absent, 'no local review'; (3) verdict records but no APPROVE → absent, 'no local approval'; Eligibility is decided before any head comparison, from the record's top-level fields as retain_verdict writes them (bin/lib/fm_evidence.py:303-307): an APPROVE record is eligible only if it has a signature and nonempty string head, base and patch; its separate `binding` object is not required and not consulted, so a signed record with complete head, base and patch qualifies with or without `binding`; signed records of either provenance level qualify. An unsigned historical record (:172-175), an empty-head legacy record (:207), and a signed record whose base or patch is missing or empty are never eligible and are ignored for selection, whatever their head. (4) eligible APPROVE records exist but none at the expected head → stale with the newest eligible one's head (a mixed history of an ineligible record at the expected head and an eligible older one is therefore stale); (5) APPROVE records exist but none is eligible → absent, 'verdict has no source binding'; (6) eligible record without a walk fence → absent, 'no walk'; (7) fence present but check fails → invalid with the category; (8) the base or head objects are missing locally so the diff cannot be computed → invalid, 'diff unavailable'; (9) otherwise valid. When several APPROVE records exist at the expected head the newest in store order is used. details.walk sits at the top level of details beside T-242's refs and is never copied into events, wakes or any other top-level pending field. Attaching never changes the verdict, the binding, the gates or the merge path. The table above governs every expected outcome; any other, unclassified attach failure yields {status: invalid, reason: 'walk check failed'} and the card is still written.

Change 6, the card's current head and staleness. A merge card is bound to its expected_head when it is raised (bin/fm-decide.sh:546-549) and the merge enforces that head; the board does not track a live PR head. So 'current head' for a card is its expected_head, and freshness is decided at attach time: only a walk from a verdict at that exact head is shown; status stale shows 'walk out of date' with the reviewed head's short sha and hides every note and step; absent/invalid shows 'no code walk for this head' with the reason. When the PR advances after the card was raised, the existing card keeps its walk labelled with its own head, and the next card for the new head carries whatever walk the new head's review has (stale after a same-patch rebase with no new review). There is no 'unknown freshness' state.

Change 7, the board (board/public/index.html, board.css, board.js, new board/public/walk.js; board/server.ts only if serving walk.js needs it). Evidence first: every card, one-way doors included, opens on T-242's evidence view. Reading order: the intent key-point list, then 'How it works' (the animation), then 'Walk the diff', then the decision bar. Loading: index.html loads walk.js lazily, only when it first renders a card or task detail that carries a scene or a walk, so a page whose cards carry neither makes exactly the requests it makes today (the asset allowlist in tests/e2e/game.spec.ts:198-205 stays unchanged). Animation: walk.js lays the scene out deterministically in the browser (lanes as columns, nodes in array order within their lane, right-angle edge paths between node sides), draws SVG, and plays before (gone edges struck through and faded), change (new nodes and paths drawn in), after, with a token travelling tokens.before then tokens.after; play, pause, a scrubber, Before/Change/After buttons; each change badge cN jumps to its blocks. It redraws from details.<locale>.scene on a locale switch and shows the T-242 before/after fallback when the scene is absent or fails to lay out. prefers-reduced-motion shows the static change view with numbered steps and no autoplay. No video or image files. Each intent row shows the badges of the changes whose intents include it; a click highlights those changes, dims the rest and plays; a banner offers 'Walk its code', which opens the walk on that intent's tab at its first key block; 'Show all' clears the highlight. 'Walk the diff' has two tabs: 'Intent check' (T-242's check, selected by default, always available) and 'Walk the code', collapsed until clicked; the one-way A unlock keeps T-242's rule exactly (every reviewed intent ticked and the correct comprehension answer, board/server.ts:1823-1841) and never requires opening the walk. Inside the walk: one tab per intent and a last tab 'Other changes'. An intent tab shows only that intent's key blocks (at most 5): the rows, the note, the line note marked on its line, and the block's step lit in the animation; ↑/↓ move between blocks and Space plays or pauses the step. 'Other changes' lists files with their remaining hunk counts and kinds, each linked to the PR diff, with no notes. No element shows a total block count. Partial data: scene only → animation and badges, 'Walk its code' disabled with 'no code walk for this head'; walk only → no animation, the T-242 fallback, intent rows link straight to their walk tab; an intent with no key block → its tab says it has no key block and its banner has no walk link; a change with no mapped block → its badge highlights but its jump is disabled; neither → exactly T-242's card. Task details (intentBody detailOnly, index.html:1301) show the scene animation from the spec explain and never a walk. All authored text (notes, line notes, labels, file paths, rows) is HTML-escaped with the existing esc().

Not changed, stated. The verdict and its parsing, the gates, merge, the door check and T-242's evidence view; bin/lib/fm_evidence.py, bin/lib/fm_merge_details.py, bin/fm-diagram.sh, board/public/diagram.js and authored diagrams; cards and specs without scene or walk render exactly as T-242 left them; the voyage game.

Tests, new behaviour. Behavioural evidence for the fail-first gate comes only from assertions that run on base d9cba7a through entry points that exist there (fm_ste.py check-explain, spec preflight, fm-decide.sh merge requests, fm-review.sh, the board) and fail there for a behavioural reason; cases that call the new fm_walk.py directly skip with an explicit setup reason when it is absent and are never counted as base failures, following tests/lib/card_refs.py (:21-27); preservation checks are listed under regression. tests/walk.test.sh with tests/lib/walk_cases.py: (a) a valid scene is accepted by `fm_ste.py check-explain` and by spec preflight (on base both refuse it as an unknown explain field); (b) each scene rule refuses with its own message: lane index out of range, duplicate id, bad change id sequence, change missing on gone/new, change present on same, unknown edge endpoint, discontinuous token path, a gone edge in tokens.after, intents out of range, a label failing label rules, a change text with two sentences, each count limit exceeded, an edge touching a gone node that is not gone, an edge touching a new node that is not new, an edge joining a gone and a new node, a counter value empty or over 12 code points or not a string, and a locale mismatch in ids, lanes, states, tokens, counter values and change intents; boundaries (6 lanes, 24 nodes, 40 edges, 9 changes, 24-edge token paths, a 12-character counter value) are accepted; (c) fm_walk check accepts a valid walk and refuses: an unknown hunk id, a hunk key for two intents, 6 key blocks for one intent, 41 in all, a missing note, a note missing one locale or carrying an extra key, a note failing STE, a line_note outside its block, step with no scene, a missing step with a scene, an unknown step id, an empty step, a block change whose intents exclude the block's intent, a malformed line_note (missing a locale, an extra key, a non-integer line, a line on the other side), proves on a code block, proves naming a test block, an intent number out of range, a repeated intent, two walk fences, invalid JSON; a missing fence is status absent; (c2) rows: a mixed replacement hunk yields typed del and add rows with both numbers; a 120-row hunk with a line note on row 110 shows an 80-row window containing it with truncated counts; (d) other is the exact complement on a synthetic diff with 400 hunks and 3 key blocks, covering a deletion-only hunk (L id), a deleted file, a binary file, a mode-only change, an empty new file and a path needing git quoting; (e) attach, through fm-decide.sh merge requests, each row (1)-(9) of the Change 5 table with the card written and exit status 0, row (1) for both an enriched and an unenriched request; the legacy cases: an empty-head legacy APPROVE alone (row 5), an unsigned historical APPROVE alone (row 5), each of the four signed source-field defects alone, missing base, empty base, missing patch and empty patch (row 5 for each), and each of those four at the expected head beside an eligible APPROVE at an older head (row 4 for each), a signed APPROVE with complete head, base and patch and no binding object at the expected head (eligible: row 6 or 9), an ineligible APPROVE at the expected head plus an eligible older one (row 4), and an eligible APPROVE at the expected head beside an unsigned one (row 6 or 9); and the lifecycle: a card raised at H1 carries a valid walk labelled H1; the PR advances to H2 with a new APPROVE and the H1 card file is byte-unchanged while a card at H2 carries the H2 walk; a same-patch rebase to H3 with no new review gives a card at H3 with status stale naming H2; (e2) an authored merge-details scene that differs from the pin refuses the request with 'scene mismatch with spec', and the autopilot deliberately treats that refusal as a generic merge-request failure: its recovery pattern (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:710) stays limited to intent/change_points/door/check because built details never carry a scene; (e3) the PR comment for a verdict with a walk contains the replacement line and no fence; a malformed walk whose note names a path produces a crew_status line with the category only; (f) scene injection: a merge request whose pin has a scene gets details.<locale>.scene equal to the pin for authored details and for details built by fm_merge_details; authored details with a different scene are refused. tests/review-evidence.test.sh: a retained verdict whose text holds a walk fence keeps its verdict, markers, standing list and signature, and the walk read from it carries that record's head, base and patch. tests/e2e/board-walk.spec.ts: the scene plays, pauses, scrubs and jumps from a badge to its blocks; an intent row highlights its changes and its banner opens that intent's first block; 'Show all' clears; the walk opens on intent tabs with at most 5 blocks each, ↑/↓ and Space work, 'Other changes' lists files and counts without notes, and no element shows a total block count; stale shows 'walk out of date' and hides notes; reduced motion shows the static view; on load the walk is collapsed on every card, and a one-way card's A unlocks from the intent ticks plus the correct comprehension answer without opening the walk, while ticks with a wrong answer stay locked; each partial-data case above; a locale switch redraws the scene; task details show the scene without a walk; a note containing markup renders as text.

Regression coverage, existing suites that must stay green unchanged unless named in scope: tests/ste.test.sh and tests/lib/ste_cases.py (:146), the spec-explain cases in tests/lib/spec_explain_cases.py (CLI, preflight and isolated configuration), bin/lib/fm_config_tasks.py explain validation, tests/card-refs.test.sh and tests/decide.test.sh (T-242 enrichment), tests/autopilot-merge-path.test.sh with tests/lib/autopilot_merge_path.py (:58-69, the builder's field list), tests/task-diagram.test.sh and tests/diagram.test.sh, tests/e2e/board-intent-cards.spec.ts (legacy intent cards), tests/e2e/board-change-points.spec.ts (:8, :21: T-242 evidence view and the one-way lock with a wrong answer) with its shared fixture tests/e2e/lib/intent-card.ts (:30), tests/lib/card_refs.py (parse_diff's default output unchanged), verdict and signature preservation in bin/lib/fm_evidence.py (:161) through tests/review-evidence.test.sh, tests/e2e/board-task-detail.spec.ts (:127 external task detail), tests/review-diff.test.sh (in scope, updated only as Change 3 states), tests/e2e/board-crew.spec.ts, tests/e2e/game.spec.ts (:198-205, the exact board request allowlist, unchanged because walk.js loads only for a scene or walk) and tests/i18n.test.sh. fm_walk.py is run only by fm-review.sh and fm-decide.sh merge requests, not by the board; if the e2e fixture must execute a merge request that loads it, add it to the helper list in tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts (:104) and to the exact listing asserted in tests/e2e/board-crew.spec.ts (:54), both in scope.

Migration of records, pins and tasks in flight. Existing evidence records and signatures, pins, pending and answered cards and prior reviews are never rewritten. A review already running under the old prompt produces no walk, so its card gets status absent and renders without a walk; an old pinned spec without a scene injects nothing and its card renders as T-242 left it; a pending card raised before this merge has no details.walk and renders as before. No repin is needed for any task. The firstmate rule 'write a scene for a spec whose flow changes' applies only to specs authored after this task merges; T-244's own explain carries no scene, because base check-explain refuses the field. Walk eligibility for old records is the eligibility rule of the Change 5 table, applied before head selection: an unsigned historical verdict or an empty-head legacy verdict never sources a walk; a signed verdict from a non-Codex adapter (provenance legacy, bin/lib/fm_evidence.py:297) does. Tests: an unsigned legacy verdict with a walk fence gives absent; a signed legacy-provenance verdict with a valid fence gives valid; a review that completes under the old prompt (verdict without a fence) gives absent; after attach, the pin file (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:194 snapshots), every verdict record and every pending and answered decision file other than the new card are byte-identical (sha256 before and after); a card with neither field, a card with a scene and no walk, and a T-242 card raised before this task render as stated, in tests/lib/walk_cases.py and tests/e2e/board-walk.spec.ts.

I18n. Every new visible string and accessible label (play, pause, scrubber, Before/Change/After, Show all, Walk its code, Walk the code, Intent check, Other changes, walk out of date, no code walk for this head, no key block, the stale head label) is looked up through a literal double-quoted t("key") call so tests/i18n.test.sh (:47-58) sees it; each key is added to i18n/ui.en.json and i18n/ui.zh-TW.json, zh-CN is derived through i18n/tw2cn.tsv, and no dynamic key names are used.

External-project privacy. For a project with FM_EXTERNAL=1 the walk is read only through the project's private evidence store (Store under fm_storage_init), the canonical diff is computed in the target clone, and nothing is written into the engine tree; scene and walk live only inside a card's details, which publicDecision (board/server.ts:802-806) already strips from answer projections and session wakes, and they are never added to events, wakes, PR comments or other public projections. The PR comment projection drops the walk fence (Change 3), and crew_status lines carry only categories. Tests: an external merge request's wake payload and decision_requested event contain no walk text or scene; under FM_EXTERNAL=1 with comments projection and project review fm, the posted comment has no fence and no note text; an external card's walk renders from its private pending record; a hunk path needing quoting is handled; notes and rows are escaped.

Docs. design/design.md, edited in place inside the numbered sections: §5.2 (the explain paragraph at :422-440: the scene schema and its locale rules), §6 (the reviewer's walk fence, hunk ids, canonical diff and the crew_status line), §8 (the card's animation, walk tabs, partial-data and staleness rules). skills/reviewer/SKILL.md: how to write the walk fence. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md (the explain guidance near :818): write a scene for every spec whose flow changes, from this task's merge onward.

intent.text: 卡片用動畫呈現邏輯在改前和改後的變化。
